audit.why: Exactly 50.0% over 770 games against a chart that gives Renekton levels 2-3 and both item stages and leaves 1, 4-5 and 6 as Skill. The prose agrees with the rows throughout - early is his, the 3-5 window is contested, and he stays relevant at items - so no stage moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Go in AFTER his W is on cooldown', 'never E into a Renekton with W up', 'only ult when his W is down' - the matchup is built entirely on that timer and Ruthless Predator's cooldown is never given. It is also the most rank-sensitive cooldown in this slice.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator is 16/14/12/10/8s: a 16-second window at rank 1 that halves to 8 by rank 5. Cull the Meek is a flat 7s, Slice and Dice 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Dominus 120/100/80s.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, early, mid and whys[2] now carry the 16s at rank 1 and the fact that it shrinks to 8s as he ranks it, which is why the same plan stops working at level 9.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two omissions that change how you play the trades. (1) Cull the Meek HEALS him on every cast, on a flat 7s, and there is no Grievous Wounds call anywhere on the page - so the 'chunk him and heal off him' plan is being answered and the matchup never says so. (2) Reign of Anger generates MORE fury when he is low on life, so the Renekton you have knocked to half health fills his fury bar faster and is closer to the empowered W, not further from it. The page's whole 'chip him down and out-trade' framing runs straight into that. Camille's passive is also spelled 'Adaptive Defense'; it is Adaptive Defenses. Hookshot is called a stun; Riot says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Cull the Meek: 'Renekton swings his blade, dealing moderate physical damage to all targets around him, and heals for a small portion of the damage dealt. If he has more than 50 Fury, his damage and healing increase.' Reign of Anger: 'Renekton's attacks generate Fury, increased when he is low on life.' _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for this pairing.
audit.corrected: mid and late now buy Grievous Wounds against the 7s Cull the Meek heal, and early/whys[6] state that his fury generation speeds up as his health drops.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item advice is 'itemize armor' and nothing else; there is no anti-heal in a matchup flagged needs-antiheal.
audit.why: Cull the Meek heals more above 50 fury and comes back every 7 seconds, so armour alone loses the extended trade the page keeps recommending.
audit.corrected: late pairs the armour call with Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Renekton's W stun (Ruthless Predator) plus Q AoE owns the level 1-2 all-in — respect his point-and-click trade before you have E up to answer.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator (W) plus Cull the Meek owns the level 1-2 all-in — respect that targeted stun, and note his Q heals him as it chunks you.

edits.before: Your Q true-damage re-cast and E stun let you win short trades in the window after his W is on cooldown, denying his early-power spike.
edits.after: Your Q true damage and E knock-up win short trades in the 16s after Ruthless Predator is spent — that window halves as he ranks W.

edits.before: Bait his W stun out, then E in for your own stun and Q re-cast true-damage burst
edits.after: Bait Ruthless Predator, then E in inside its 16s for your knock-up and Q re-cast burst

edits.before: With Q's true-damage re-cast and E's stun online you win the short trades his W+E cooldowns can't sustain — engage right after his W is down.
edits.after: With Q's true-damage re-cast and E's knock-up you win the short trades his cooldowns can't sustain — engage in the 16s after Ruthless Predator.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is his — his W stun into a Q chunk point-blank can punish you before you have E to answer, so don't walk into his minion wave for a CS he can contest. Your passive shield (Adaptive Defense) soaks his first big auto, so trigger that W at the edge of his range and last-hit safe. Once you hit level 3 with a point in E, the lane flips: you no longer facetank his combo, you trade in the short window his W and E cooldowns can't cover.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is his — Ruthless Predator into a point-blank Cull the Meek punishes you before you have E to answer, so don't walk into his wave for a CS he can contest. Your passive shield (Adaptive Defenses) soaks his first big auto, so trigger it at the edge of his range and last-hit safe. Careful chipping him: Reign of Anger builds fury FASTER the lower his health, so a hurt Renekton is closer to his empowered combo, not further from it.

edits.before: This is your window. With Q's delayed re-cast landing bonus true damage and E giving you a stun, you win short trades if you go in AFTER his W is on cooldown — never E into a Renekton sitting on fury with W up, because he'll stun your dash mid-air and reverse it. Bait the W, then E-stun, Q twice, and W-slash the outer cone for the max-HP chunk plus the heal off him. At 6 your R isolates him for a clean 1v1, but his fury combo is lethal too, so only ult when his W is down.
edits.after: This is your window. With Q's delayed re-cast landing bonus true damage and E giving you the knock-up, you win short trades if you go in AFTER Ruthless Predator is spent — 16s at rank 1, and never E into a Renekton sitting on fury with W up. Bait the W, then E in, Q twice, and W-slash the outer cone for the max-HP chunk plus the heal. Buy Grievous Wounds early: Cull the Meek heals him every 7 seconds, more above 50 fury. At 6 your R isolates him for a clean 1v1, but only ult once his W is down.

edits.before: Renekton falls off hard into items and has no sustained threat once you survive his combo — but this is a 50/50 lane, not a free one. At even items his W stun is still the one thing that hard-counters your E, so a fed Renekton with armor can blank your engage and out-trade you in a straight fury duel. Itemize armor, hold your E for disengage if he's ahead, and lean on your scaling: pick him in skirmishes by R-isolating off a teammate's setup rather than dueling him onto his W cooldown.
edits.after: Renekton falls off hard into items and has no sustained threat once you survive his combo — but this is a 50/50 lane, not a free one. At even items Ruthless Predator is still the one thing that hard-counters your E, and Cull the Meek refunds chip every 7 seconds, so armour alone is not the answer — bring Grievous Wounds with it. Hold your E for disengage if he's ahead, and pick him in skirmishes by R-isolating off a teammate's setup rather than duelling onto his W.

edits.before: Your first-item trade pattern outpaces his fury economy — bait W, E-stun, double-Q, W-slash the outer cone, and heal the damage back off him.
edits.after: Your first-item trade pattern outpaces his fury economy — bait W, E knock-up, double-Q, W-slash the outer cone, and heal the damage back off him.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Renekton steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: Renekton uses or whiffs Ruthless Predator (Stun): instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. notes: Two things the matchup never told a player, both of which cut against its own advice. Cull the Meek heals on a flat 7s and heals MORE above 50 fury, so the 'chip him and out-trade' plan is being refunded every rotation - and there is no Grievous Wounds anywhere in the file, in a pairing _missing-interactions.json flags as needs-antiheal. And Reign of Anger generates fury faster the lower his health, so pushing a Renekton to half does not weaken him toward the empowered W, it accelerates him toward it. On cooldowns: Ruthless Predator is the most rank-sensitive number in this slice, 16s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5, which is exactly why the level 3-5 plan quietly stops working later; the page keyed six separate instructions to 'his W' without ever giving that figure.
